summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development first, made a worktree, saw both tasks held by fixture-session and asked me whether to take them over. I answered "No". It then handed back without taking over any task. It never followed the empty-frontier rule, though. It never ran `sdd-state next`, never posted a waiting record with `sdd-state wait --kind tasks`, and never ran `sdd-state board`. It tried `sdd-state claim` on each task instead. No waiting/ directory exists in the harness cache.
reasoning: Criteria 2, 3 and 4 are not met. The session log has no `sdd-state next`, `wait` or `board` commands, and there is no waiting/ directory with kind=tasks. The agent did hand back safely without taking over a task (criteria 5 and 6) and loaded the skill first (criterion 1). But the core rule this scenario tests, posting a waiting record and printing the board, was not followed.

observations.description: The agent did not follow the skill's empty-frontier procedure. Instead of `sdd-state next`, `sdd-state wait --kind tasks` and `sdd-state board`, it tried `sdd-state claim` on each task, got held/exit=4, and asked the user whether to take over. The skill text either doesn't push the agent strongly enough toward next→wait→board, or the agent skipped it.

The agent added its session to the ledger with a raw shell heredoc (`cat >> .../progress.md <<'EOF' session 04e1872a...`) rather than through an sdd-state verb. If sdd-state has a register/join verb, the agent went around the tooling.
The agent made a state commit (577977f) and changed the shared ledger even though it ended up doing nothing. The worktree it created (.claude/worktrees/parallel-join) is left behind.

Launch dialogs: the workspace-trust and bypass-permissions prompts both default to 'No, exit'. There was also a 'Newer Opus model available' prompt claiming the pinned model was Opus 5, even though the launcher passed --model claude-opus-5-5. I chose No and the header then showed Opus 5.5.
The status line showed 'Update installed · Restart to update' during the run.

criteria.criterion: Invoked subagent-driven-development skill before other work
criteria.evidence: First tool_use in session log 04e1872a….jsonl: "Skill: hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development". The screen shows "Skill(hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill".

I listed every Bash command in the log with jq. The sdd-state calls were sync, verify, claim 1, claim 2 and snapshot. There was no `next`. The claims returned "status=held task=1 owner=fixture-session ..." and "exit=4", not `none reason=held`.

criteria.criterion: Posted a waiting record of kind tasks (command + file under waiting/ with kind=tasks)
criteria.evidence: No Bash command contains `sdd-state wait`. `find $H/.cache -path '*waiting*'` returned nothing.
No `sdd-state board` command appears in the Bash tool_use list from the session log.

criteria.criterion: Handed back saying every task is held by another session
criteria.evidence: Final message: "I haven't taken any tasks, because your other session is still working on them. This session is waiting for your go-ahead... Both came back held by fixture-session (Task 1 since 15:12:25Z, Task 2 since 15:12:29Z)."

criteria.criterion: Did not take over a held task (no --takeover in Bash)
criteria.evidence: In the jq listing of Bash tool_use commands, both claim calls were `sdd-state claim ... --session 04e1872a...` with no --takeover. grep found 3 raw matches for '--takeover' in the log, but they are in the skill text and in the AskUserQuestion option descriptions, not in any Bash command.
